answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it earns, like a falcon proving its hunting ground before it flies: the stake stays locked, and duplicate or fake identities lose it when overlapping behaviour is detected. Reputation then grows slowly and cannot be bought in bulk, so a flood of cheap velvet copies cannot outvote real workers. At its nadir, an attacker faces a simple cost: every fake identity costs real funds, while honest agents keep stake and reputation.
